name: Randomization
short: Let chance decide who gets what.
text: Let chance decide who gets what. Balances known and unknown confounders, on average.

ref.cite: Altman & Bland (1999). Statistics notes: How to randomise. BMJ.

name: Allocation concealment
short: No one can see or steer the next assignment.
text: Nobody enrolling participants can know or influence the next assignment.

ref.cite: Schulz et al. (1995). Empirical evidence of bias: dimensions of methodological quality associated with estimates of treatment effects in controlled trials. JAMA.

name: Blinding
short: Nobody knows who got what.
text: Participants, clinicians, outcome assessors or analysts don't know who got what, or what the hypothesis is.

ref.cite: Schulz & Grimes (2002). Blinding in randomised trials: hiding who got what. The Lancet.

name: Placebo or sham control
short: The control arm gets an identical-looking dummy.
text: The control group gets an indistinguishable dummy, so expectations are equal in both arms.

ref.cite: Beecher (1955). The powerful placebo. Journal of the American Medical Association.

name: Intention-to-treat
short: Analyse everyone as randomized, whatever happened next.
text: Analyse everyone in the group they were randomized to, whatever happened next; handle missing data explicitly.

ref.cite: Hollis & Campbell (1999). What is meant by intention to treat analysis? Survey of published randomised controlled trials. BMJ.

name: Preregistration
short: Lock in the plan before you see the data.
text: Publish hypotheses, primary outcome and analysis plan (or review protocol) before seeing the data.

ref.cite: Nosek et al. (2018). The preregistration revolution. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

name: Sample-size planning
short: Work out how many you need before you start.
text: Work out in advance how many units you need to detect the smallest effect that matters.

ref.cite: Cohen (1992). A power primer. Psychological Bulletin.

name: Causal diagram (DAG)
short: Draw the causal map; adjust only for what belongs.
text: Draw your causal assumptions; adjust for confounders, and deliberately not for colliders or mediators.

ref.cite: Greenland et al. (1999). Causal Diagrams for Epidemiologic Research. Epidemiology.

name: Matching / propensity scores
short: Compare like with like.
text: Compare treated and untreated units that are similar on measured characteristics.

ref.cite: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983). The central role of the propensity score in observational studies for causal effects. Biometrika.

name: Negative controls
short: Test something that should show no effect.
text: Test an exposure or outcome that can't plausibly be linked; any 'effect' there exposes hidden bias.

ref.cite: Lipsitch et al. (2010). Negative Controls. Epidemiology.

name: Sensitivity analysis
short: Change the assumptions. Does the answer survive?
text: Re-run under different assumptions (missing data, unmeasured confounding, E-values, model choices). Do conclusions survive?

ref.cite: VanderWeele & Ding (2017). Sensitivity Analysis in Observational Research: Introducing the E-Value. Annals of Internal Medicine.

name: Active comparator, new users
short: Compare new users of one treatment with new users of another.
text: Compare new users of a treatment with new users of an alternative for the same indication.

ref.cite: Ray (2003). Evaluating Medication Effects Outside of Clinical Trials: New-User Designs. American Journal of Epidemiology.

name: Time-zero alignment
short: Everyone's clock starts at the same moment.
text: Start follow-up when eligibility is met and the treatment strategy is assigned, the same moment for everyone.

ref.cite: Hernán et al. (2016). Specifying a target trial prevents immortal time bias and other self-inflicted injuries in observational analyses. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology.

name: Lag & early-event exclusion
short: Leave a gap between exposure and outcome.
text: Measure exposure long before the outcome, or set aside early events, to blunt reverse causation.

ref.cite: Tamim et al. (2007). Application of lag-time into exposure definitions to control for protopathic bias. Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety.

name: Concurrent control group
short: A comparison group living through the same period.
text: Compare against a group measured over the same period, so trends and regression to the mean hit both equally.

ref.cite: Pocock (1976). The combination of randomized and historical controls in clinical trials. Journal of Chronic Diseases.

name: Pre-trend check & control series
short: Show the groups moved together before the change.
text: Show the groups moved in parallel before the intervention, or add a comparison series it couldn't have affected.

ref.cite: Roth et al. (2023). What’s trending in difference-in-differences? A synthesis of the recent econometrics literature. Journal of Econometrics.

name: Allocate by cluster
short: Assign whole groups, so nothing leaks between arms.
text: Assign whole groups (classes, wards, villages) so the intervention can't leak into the control group.

ref.cite: Donner & Klar (2004). Pitfalls of and Controversies in Cluster Randomization Trials. American Journal of Public Health.

name: Washout period
short: Let the first treatment wear off.
text: Leave enough time between treatment periods for the previous effect to disappear.

ref.cite: Wellek & Blettner (2012). On the Proper Use of the Crossover Design in Clinical Trials. Deutsches Ärzteblatt international.

name: External validation
short: Test it on data it has never seen.
text: Test the model or method on data from another time or place that it has never seen.

ref.cite: Altman & Royston (2000). What do we mean by validating a prognostic model?. Statistics in Medicine.

name: Multiplicity correction
short: Name one primary outcome, or pay for every extra test.
text: Name one primary outcome, or adjust for the number of tests you run.

ref.cite: Benjamini & Hochberg (1995). Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology.

name: Independent replication
short: Someone else does it again.
text: Another team, sample or site repeats the study, ideally with the same pre-registered plan.

ref.cite: Open Science Collaboration (2015). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. Science.

name: Comprehensive search
short: Search everywhere, including the drawers.
text: Search multiple databases, trial registries, preprints and grey literature, and contact authors.

ref.cite: Bramer et al. (2017). Optimal database combinations for literature searches in systematic reviews: a prospective exploratory study. Systematic Reviews.

name: Grey-literature appraisal
short: Grade every grey source before you trust it.
text: Score each grey source for its producer's authority, stated method, objectivity, date and outlet tier, and set stopping rules for the search in advance.

ref.cite: Garousi, Felderer & Mäntylä (2019). Guidelines for including grey literature and conducting multivocal literature reviews in software engineering. Information and Software Technology.

name: Pre-planned heterogeneity analysis
short: Plan in advance how you'll explain why studies differ.
text: Random-effects models plus pre-specified subgroups and meta-regression to explore why studies differ.

ref.cite: Sun et al. (2010). Is a subgroup effect believable? Updating criteria to evaluate the credibility of subgroup analyses. BMJ.

name: Representative sampling
short: Sample from the whole population, not the convenient part.
text: Recruit from a defined population (all consecutive patients, a random sample), not whoever is convenient.

ref.cite: Neyman (1934). On the Two Different Aspects of the Representative Method: The Method of Stratified Sampling and the Method of Purposive Selection. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society.

name: Validated, objective measures
short: Use instruments proven to measure what matters.
text: Use calibrated instruments, records or validated scales instead of memory or ad-hoc questions, and outcomes that matter rather than unvalidated surrogates.

ref.cite: Mokkink et al. (2010). The COSMIN study reached international consensus on taxonomy, terminology, and definitions of measurement properties for health-related patient-reported outcomes. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology.

name: Reflexivity & double coding
short: Write down your own lens, and let a second coder check.
text: Keep an audit trail and reflexive notes, have a second analyst code independently, check interpretations with participants.

ref.cite: Malterud (2001). Qualitative research: standards, challenges, and guidelines. The Lancet.

name: Triangulation
short: Different methods, different flaws, same answer.
text: Combine sources, methods or designs with different weaknesses. Trust the conclusions they agree on.

ref.cite: Lawlor et al. (2017). Triangulation in aetiological epidemiology. International Journal of Epidemiology.

name: Theoretical sampling to saturation
short: Keep sampling until nothing new turns up.
text: Keep adding cases chosen to challenge emerging ideas, until new data add nothing new.

ref.cite: Guest et al. (2006). How Many Interviews Are Enough?. Field Methods.

name: Multilevel analysis
short: Model people inside groups inside places.
text: Model individuals nested in groups, using individual-level data wherever possible.

ref.cite: Diez Roux (2002). A glossary for multilevel analysis. Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health.

name: Verification & validation
short: Check the code is right, then check the model matches reality.
text: Verify that the code solves the equations correctly (convergence tests, unit checks); validate the model against real experiments.

ref.cite: Oberkampf & Trucano (2002). Verification and validation in computational fluid dynamics. Progress in Aerospace Sciences.

name: Multi-site, diverse sample
short: Run it where the results will be used.
text: Run the study across the settings and populations where the results will actually be used.

ref.cite: Rothwell (2005). External validity of randomised controlled trials: “To whom do the results of this trial apply?”. The Lancet.

name: Self or sibling comparison
short: Compare people with themselves, or siblings with siblings.
text: Compare units with themselves, or siblings with each other, so stable background factors cancel out.

ref.cite: Lahey & D'Onofrio (2010). All in the Family: Comparing Siblings to Test Causal Hypotheses Regarding Environmental Influences on Behavior. Current Directions in Psychological Science.

name: Run charts & control limits
short: Judge a change against the process's own baseline variation.
text: Plot the measure over time from a stable baseline and apply pre-set rules (shifts, trends, control limits), so real change stands out from noise and drift.

ref.cite: Benneyan (2003). Statistical process control as a tool for research and healthcare improvement. Quality and Safety in Health Care.
